statement: WORKPACK_INDEX.md line for arc-13 explicitly labels the fold as SKELETON, with the note '(skeleton; e01 owns src/bridge.rs)'. The Requirement Checklist inside arc-13-enforcer-literal-scan.md itself does NOT repeat this split -- it reads as if arc-13 alone must 'expose results as enforcer-domain Findings via the validator/scan interface'. Trusting only the workpack body (per the read-only-this-workpack stop rule) would lead a worker to implement the enforcer-validator::Validator bridge (src/bridge.rs) itself, duplicating e01's owned file and creating a cross-lane collision.
why: The workpack's own text and WORKPACK_INDEX.md disagree on scope boundary (bridge.rs in-or-out), and the stop rule forbids reading sibling workpacks (which would have surfaced e01's ownership directly). WORKPACK_INDEX.md is not a sibling workpack -- it is the index -- so cross-checking it against the requirement checklist before writing a validator-trait adapter is the only way to catch this without violating the stop rule.
howToApply: For any arc-1x crate workpack, always grep its own row in WORKPACK_INDEX.md (not just full-read the workpack file) before starting -- the index's 'owns' column and inline parenthetical notes (e.g. '(skeleton; e01 owns src/bridge.rs)') are the authoritative scope-split signal when the workpack body is silent or ambiguous about a boundary. Do not infer scope from the workpack's prose alone when a checklist item sounds like it spans two crates.

evidence.ref: docs/plans/enforcer-selfhost-plan/WORKPACK_INDEX.md line for arc-13: 'crates/enforcer-literal-scan/**, Tools/ocentra-literal-scan/** (skeleton; e01 owns src/bridge.rs)'; docs/plans/enforcer-selfhost-plan/workpacks/e01-literal-scan-universal-t2.md row: 'crates/enforcer-literal-scan/src/bridge.rs, tests/fixtures/universal/**, tests/bridge.rs ... owns the bridge.rs file arc-13 skeleton excludes'

statement: The standalone Tools/ocentra-literal-scan tool (62 source files, 15 tests, ~10 lexer helper functions sharing a cursor-state signature: source/out/index/line/col/...) was written and tested outside this workspace's [workspace.lints] deny-wall (unwrap_used/expect_used/print_stdout/print_stderr/map_err_ignore/needless_pass_by_value/too_many_arguments all deny by default here). Moving it in as-is triggered ~30 clippy errors and required a crate-level #![allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] (systemic to the inherited lexer family, ~10 call sites) plus test-file-level #![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used)] in both lib_tests.rs's #[cfg(test)] mod attribute and tests/integration.rs's crate attribute, plus real fixes for print_stdout/print_stderr (scoped #[allow] on the 3 CLI-output functions, since a CLI's stdout IS its contract), map_err_ignore (2 sites -- interpolate the source error instead of `|_|`), needless_pass_by_value (parse_args took Vec<String> but only ever borrowed it -- changed to &[String]), and manual_contains (1 site).
why: A worker folding ANY standalone tool/vendored crate into this workspace should expect the workspace's clippy deny-wall to surface a batch of findings the source never had to satisfy, and should budget time for it rather than being surprised mid-fold. The workspace's established pattern (confirmed via enforcer-coordination/enforcer-harness/enforcer-lang-security precedent) is scoped #[allow] with a one-line justification comment at the exact function/module, not a workspace-wide lint downgrade -- crate-level #![allow] is acceptable ONLY when the same lint fires systemically across many call sites sharing one inherited architecture (here: the lexer cursor-state signature), not for scattered incidental debt.
howToApply: When folding a standalone/vendored tool into this workspace: run `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` immediately after the raw file move (before touching anything else) to get the full deny-wall diff in one pass; triage each finding as either a real 2-minute fix (map_err_ignore, needless_pass_by_value, manual_contains are almost always trivial real fixes) or a scoped #[allow] with justification (unwrap_used/expect_used in test code, print_stdout/print_stderr in a CLI's own output layer, too_many_arguments when systemic to an inherited signature).

evidence.ref: cargo clippy -p enforcer-literal-scan --all-targets -- -D warnings: 30 errors pre-fix (7 too_many_arguments, 2 manual_unwrap_or_default, 1 manual_contains, 2 map_err_ignore, 1 needless_pass_by_value, ~15 unwrap_used/expect_used in test code, 2 print_stdout/print_stderr sites) -> 0 errors post-fix; proof/cargo/arc-13.txt captures the clean run

statement: The standalone tool's internal Finding struct (Tools/ocentra-literal-scan/src/models.rs) is intentionally richer than enforcer_domain::findings::Finding: it carries column, literal_kind, literal_preview, literal_hash, category (RiskCategory enum), score (u8 0-100), confidence, blocking (bool), reason, suggestion, context -- fields the T2 scored-scanner needs for its own report/CLI output that enforcer-domain's five-field Finding (ruleId/severity/title/detail/file/line/snippet) does not model. arc-13's SKELETON scope (see mem-arc-13-0001) does NOT require collapsing this richer internal type down to enforcer_domain::Finding -- that conversion is e01 bridge.rs's job (converting rich internal Finding -> enforcer_domain::Finding at the Validator trait boundary, necessarily lossy/summarizing).
why: A worker who read only the workpack's checklist line 'retarget its types to enforcer-domain' without cross-checking the SKELETON/bridge split (mem-arc-13-0001) could spend significant effort collapsing the internal Finding's 11 fields down to enforcer-domain's 6, discarding score/category/confidence/literal_hash data the T2 scanner's own CLI/report output still needs -- and that work would be redone/reverted when e01 lands the real bridge.
howToApply: For a SKELETON-labeled fold-in workpack, 'retarget to enforcer-domain' should be read narrowly: use enforcer-domain/enforcer-core as Cargo dependencies (so the crate is positioned to build the bridge later) without necessarily changing every internal struct's field types yet, UNLESS the workpack's own body names specific fields/types to change. Leave richer internal DTOs alone when a named sibling pack owns the conversion boundary.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-literal-scan/src/models.rs Finding struct (11 fields: rule_id,severity,file,line,column,language,file_role,literal_kind,literal_preview,literal_hash,category,score,confidence,blocking,reason,suggestion,context) vs crates/enforcer-domain/src/findings.rs Finding struct (6 fields: rule_id,severity,title,detail,file,line,snippet)
